alerts.name: postgres_replica_lag_high
alerts.title: PostgreSQL replica lag high
alerts.remediation: Check network, standby I/O, and whether the primary is flooding WAL.
alerts.sql: select application_name, client_addr::text as client_addr, extract(epoch from replay_lag)::int as replay_lag_seconds from pg_stat_replication where replay_lag is not null and replay_lag >= interval '30 seconds'

alerts.name: postgres_replica_replay_paused
alerts.title: PostgreSQL replay paused
alerts.message_template:
PostgreSQL: recovery replay is paused on this standby.

{all_rows}
alerts.remediation: SELECT pg_wal_replay_resume(); if paused on purpose, silence this alert.
alerts.sql: select pid, application_name from pg_stat_activity where backend_type = 'startup' and pg_is_in_recovery() and pg_get_wal_replay_pause_state() = 'paused'

alerts.name: postgres_logical_slot_inactive
alerts.title: PostgreSQL inactive logical slot
alerts.message_template:
PostgreSQL: {rows} inactive logical slot(s) retaining WAL.

{all_rows}
alerts.remediation: Fix the consumer or DROP the slot before disk fills.
alerts.sql: select slot_name, plugin, wal_status, active from pg_replication_slots where slot_type = 'logical' and active = false

alerts.name: mssql_hadr_replica_unhealthy
alerts.title: SQL Server AG replica unhealthy
alerts.remediation: Check Always On dashboard, endpoints, and quorum.
alerts.sql: select ar.replica_server_name, ars.role_desc, ars.operational_state_desc, ars.connected_state_desc, ars.synchronization_health_desc from sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states ars join sys.availability_replicas ar on ar.replica_id = ars.replica_id where ars.synchronization_health_desc <> 'HEALTHY' or ars.connected_state_desc <> 'CONNECTED'

alerts.name: mssql_agent_job_failed
alerts.title: SQL Server Agent job failed
alerts.message_template:
MSSQL: {rows} Agent job(s) failed on last run.

{all_rows}
alerts.remediation: Open Agent history for the job and fix the failing step.
alerts.sql: select j.name as job_name, h.run_date, h.run_time, left(h.message, 200) as message from msdb.dbo.sysjobs j cross apply (select top 1 run_status, run_date, run_time, message from msdb.dbo.sysjobhistory where job_id = j.job_id and step_id = 0 order by run_date desc, run_time desc) h where j.enabled = 1 and h.run_status = 0

alerts.name: mssql_active_blocking
alerts.title: SQL Server active blocking
alerts.remediation: Identify the blocker head and the object; kill only if safe.
alerts.sql: select session_id, blocking_session_id, wait_time as wait_time_ms, wait_type from sys.dm_exec_requests where blocking_session_id <> 0 and wait_time >= 5000

alerts.name: mariadb_replica_io_not_running
alerts.title: MariaDB replica IO not running
alerts.message_template:
MariaDB: replica IO thread is not running.

{all_rows}
alerts.remediation: Check SHOW REPLICA STATUS and network/credentials to the primary.
